angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 484,207 km at 112.53 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.8865 +/- 0.0146 mas (same row, RUWE 1.06): 112.53 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.696 +/- 0.023 solar radii from Howard et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-62 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..278...52H/abstract): 484,207 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.67 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Howard et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-62 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..278...52H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4455 +/- 70 K from Howard et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-62 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..278...52H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Howard et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-62 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..278...52H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-62.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.579, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
